{{Short description|American professor of biology (b.1951)}}
'''Mark W. Denny''' (born 1951) <ref name="NYPL_AirWater">{{cite web |title=Air and water : the biology and physics of life's media |url=https://www.nypl.org/research/research-catalog/bib/b11908242 |website=New York Public Library Research Catalog |access-date=31 December 2025}}</ref>  is a professor of biology at [[Stanford University]]. His research applies biomechanics, fluid dynamics, and probability to problems in marine ecology, particularly the physical constraints experienced by organisms living on wave-swept rocky shores.<ref name="Maelstrom1987">{{cite journal |last=Denny |first=Mark W. |title=Life in the maelstrom: The biomechanics of wave-swept rocky shores |journal=Trends in Ecology & Evolution |date=March 1987 |volume=2 |issue=3 |pages=61–66 |doi=10.1016/0169-5347(87)90150-9|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref name="AmSci1995">{{cite journal |last=Denny |first=Mark |title=Survival in the Surf Zone |journal=American Scientist |volume=83 |issue=2 |date=March–April 1995 |pages=166–173 |publisher=Sigma Xi, The Scientific Research Society |url=https://colsa.unh.edu/sites/default/files/media/2022/07/denny1995amerscisurvivalsurfzone.pdf |access-date=31 December 2025}}</ref>

His research on the [[intertidal zone]] of wave-swept shores has led to increased understanding of this habitat. His most publicized research is his work on locomotion of [[water striders]], which led to the coining of the term "[[Denny's paradox]]" to explain a discrepancy between capillary-wave-based propulsion models and the observed performance of juvenile water striders.<ref name="MIT2003">{{cite web |title=MIT leaps to solution of walking-on-water mystery |url=https://news.mit.edu/2003/robostrider |website=MIT News |publisher=Massachusetts Institute of Technology |date=1 August 2003 |access-date=31 December 2025}}</ref><ref name="JEB2004Paradox">{{cite journal |last=Denny |first=Mark W. |title=Paradox lost: answers and questions about walking on water |journal=Journal of Experimental Biology |date=15 April 2004 |volume=207 |issue=10 |pages=1601–1606 |doi=10.1242/jeb.00908}}</ref>

In 2008 he examined [[greyhound]]s, thoroughbred [[horse]]s and human athletes trying to find their maximum [[Footspeed|running speed]].<ref>{{cite journal  | author = Mark W. Denny | title = Limits to running speed in dogs, horses and humans | journal = Journal of Experimental Biology | year = 2008 | volume = 211 | issue = 24 | pages = 3836–3849 | doi = 10.1242/jeb.024968 | pmid = 19043056 | s2cid = 17484275 | url = http://jeb.biologists.org/cgi/reprint/211/24/3836.pdf | accessdate = 2008-12-02}}</ref> He predicted the fastest possible time for men's [[100 metres]] will be 9.48 seconds.<ref>{{cite magazine | last = Robson | first = David | title = Perfect athlete's 100m sprint time calculated | magazine = [[New Scientist]] | date = 2008-11-28 | url = https://www.newscientist.com/article/dn16160-perfect-athletes-100m-sprint-time-calculated.html | accessdate = 2008-12-02}}</ref>
Denny has served on the editorial board of the ''Journal of Experimental Biology''.<ref name="JEBBoard">{{cite web |title=Editors and Board |url=https://journals.biologists.com/jeb/pages/edboard |website=Journal of Experimental Biology |publisher=The Company of Biologists |access-date=31 December 2025}}</ref>

== Education and career ==
According to an ''American Scientist'' author biography, Denny received his bachelor's degree in zoology at [[Duke University]], completed graduate studies at the [[University of British Columbia]], and held postdoctoral positions at the [[University of Washington]] and the Smithsonian Tropical Research Institute.<ref name="AmSci1995" />
The same source places him at [[Stanford University]] and affiliated with [[Hopkins Marine Station]] in Pacific Grove, California.<ref name="AmSci1995" />

== Books ==
Denny has authored or co-authored several books, including:
* ''Biology and the Mechanics of the Wave-Swept Environment'' (1988).<ref name="WaveSwept1988">{{cite book |last=Denny |first=Mark W. |title=Biology and the mechanics of the wave-swept environment |publisher=Princeton University Press |year=1988 |url=https://archive.org/details/biologymechanics0000denn |access-date=31 December 2025}}</ref>
* ''Air and Water: The Biology and Physics of Life's Media'' (1993).<ref name="NYPL_AirWater" />
* ''Chance in Biology: Using Probability to Explore Nature'' (with [[Steven D. Gaines]]) (2000)..<ref name="ChanceNYPL">{{cite web |title=Chance in biology : using probability to explore nature |url=https://www.nypl.org/research/research-catalog/bib/pb9936832533506421 |website=New York Public Library Research Catalog |access-date=31 December 2025}}</ref>
* ''Conversations with Marco Polo: The Remarkable Life of Eugene C. Haderlie'' (with Joanna Lee Nelson) (2006).<ref name="MarcoPolo2006">{{cite web |title=Conversations with Marco Polo : the remarkable life of Eugene C. Haderlie |url=https://catalog.cclsny.org/cgi-bin/koha/opac-detail.pl?biblionumber=518176 |website=Chautauqua-Cattaraugus Library System catalog |access-date=31 December 2025}}</ref>
* ''How the Ocean Works: An Introduction to Oceanography'' (2008).<ref name="OceanWorksIA">{{cite book |last=Denny |first=Mark |title=How the ocean works : an introduction to oceanography |publisher=Princeton University Press |year=2008 |url=https://archive.org/details/howoceanworksint0000denn_c7j8 |access-date=31 December 2025}}</ref>
* ''Ecological Mechanics: Principles of Life's Physical Interactions'' (published 2015; ©2016).<ref name="EcoMechPUL">{{cite web |title=Ecological Mechanics : Principles of Life's Physical Interactions / Mark Denny |url=https://catalog.princeton.edu/catalog/99125212290706421 |website=Princeton University Library Catalog |access-date=31 December 2025}}</ref>

As editor:
* ''Encyclopedia of Tidepools and Rocky Shores'' (with [[Steven D. Gaines]]) (2007).<ref name="TidepoolsUCP">{{cite web |title=Encyclopedia of Tidepools and Rocky Shores |url=https://www.ucpress.edu/books/encyclopedia-of-tidepools-and-rocky-shores/pdf |website=University of California Press |access-date=31 December 2025}}</ref>
